headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: OpenHands can read/write mounted files and use MCP, while cognee handles customer/personal/finance data and allowlisted egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can use MCP and read/write runtime files, so it may ingest cognee outputs through a shared workspace or server channel. Cognee’s session-memory and document/data handling make it plausible that its outputs are treated as trusted content. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and escalated from low to medium.
conditions: IF cognee writes instructions or data into files mounted into OpenHands' runtime, OpenHands may parse them as actionable content.
IF an MCP server bridges the two agents without provenance checks, prompt injection becomes feasible.
mitigations: Disable shared MCP endpoints between the agents.
Separate their filesystems; do not mount cognee outputs into OpenHands.
Add a provenance tag and manual review step before OpenHands consumes cognee-generated text.
Restrict OpenHands to read-only access for any shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches customer support, personal, and finance data, while OpenHands can read files in its runtime and has broad network egress. If any sensitive cognee artifacts are mounted into OpenHands, OpenHands can transmit them to external services or model providers. The pairwise leakage path is therefore dangerous by default once data is shared.
conditions: IF cognee outputs containing personal or finance data are mounted into OpenHands' runtime, OpenHands can read them.
IF OpenHands sends runtime contents to a configured model provider or external API, those data can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Do not mount sensitive cognee data into OpenHands.
Use separate tenants or isolated workspaces for each agent.
Block outbound network from OpenHands when handling sensitive artifacts.
Redact personal and finance fields before any handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP and egress allowlists at the runtime boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cognee has session-scoped memory and OpenHands can write files, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses in a shared runtime. If both operate on the same mounted workspace, concurrent writes or git mutations can overwrite each other and corrupt state. The overlap is broad and dangerous in default OpenHands-style runtimes.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same mounted directory, file-write races can occur.
IF OpenHands modifies git state while cognee updates artifacts in the same workspace, conflicts can corrupt history or outputs.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace directory.
Disable git writes in OpenHands for shared projects.
Serialize write access with a simple lock file or queue.
Use read-only mounts for cognee inputs consumed by OpenHands.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking and conflict resolution.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations that OpenHands can consume as files or MCP-fed context. OpenHands can then act on that content with shell, browser, and git tools. The pair creates a plausible unverified handoff where one agent’s output becomes the other’s authority, but no direct automation chain is documented.
conditions: IF OpenHands is instructed to execute tasks derived from cognee-generated decisions without review, errors can cascade into actions.
IF cognee outputs incorrect workflow patterns that OpenHands commits or runs, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require human approval before OpenHands acts on cognee outputs.
Add a verification checklist for facts and citations before execution.
Limit OpenHands to drafting changes, not applying them automatically.
Keep cognee outputs as suggestions, not authoritative instructions.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates before shell, browser, or git actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal and finance data, while OpenHands runs in a Docker runtime with broad egress and model-provider API keys. If regulated data is handed from cognee to OpenHands, residency and retention obligations can be violated, especially because OpenHands may transmit runtime contents externally. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises at the pair boundary.
conditions: IF EU personal data or finance data from cognee is processed inside OpenHands, residency or retention controls may be breached.
IF OpenHands forwards runtime contents to a non-approved model provider, compliance obligations can fail.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of OpenHands.
Use a DPA-approved, region-appropriate model provider.
Shorten retention by deleting shared artifacts after use.
Log and review every cross-agent data transfer.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and retention enforcement.
